title: Distance to Equator: How Far From 0° Are You?

summary_sentence: For example, New York at 40.71°N is about 4,509 km (2,802 miles) of meridian arc from the equator, while Quito, Ecuador sits just 20 km from it.
quick_answer: The Distance to Equator tool measures the north-south distance between your latitude and 0 degrees. Enter a place or a latitude and read the distance in kilometres or miles, worked out along the meridian — the shortest route to the Earth's midline.

popular_table.intro: Meridian-arc distances computed on WGS84 — latitude converted with the ellipsoid's own degree lengths, not a flat 111 km rule.
popular_table.note: Distances are north-south arc along the meridian — the shortest route to 0°. One degree of latitude is about 110.6 km near the equator and 111.7 km near the poles on WGS84, which is why these figures are computed per latitude.

faq: By converting the latitude difference into meridian arc on the WGS84 ellipsoid. A degree of latitude is not a fixed length — it grows slightly toward the poles — so the tool integrates the local degree length rather than multiplying by a single constant.
Is it the distance to the nearest point on the equator?
Yes. The nearest point on the equator shares your longitude, so the shortest path is along your meridian — due north or due south.
Does my longitude change the answer?
No. Only latitude matters for this distance. Two places on the same parallel — say New York and Madrid — are the same distance from the equator however far apart they sit east-west.
What is the farthest a place can be from the equator?
The poles: about 10,002 km of meridian arc, a quarter of Earth's polar circumference of roughly 40,008 km.
Why does the equator matter for climate?
Solar energy per square metre peaks near the equator and falls with latitude. Distance from 0° is a rough but honest proxy for that gradient — it explains daylight patterns, not local weather.
Can I measure from a point at sea?
Yes — latitude works anywhere on Earth. A ship at 20°S in the Atlantic is about 2,212 km from the equator whether or not land is near.
How does this differ from distance to the poles?
They are complementary: distance to the equator plus distance to your nearest pole adds up to the full quadrant arc of about 10,002 km.
Which cities sit almost exactly on the equator?
Quito (Ecuador), Pontianak (Indonesia) and Macapá (Brazil) are the famous near-zero cases — each within about 25 km of the line.
